questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the functions of money is/are true?

1. Money as a unit of account means it is a standard numerical unit of measurement of the market value of goods, services and other transactions.

2. Money as a standard of deferred payment is not a significant function because modern economies rarely use money for future payments.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Money as a unit of account means it is a standard numerical unit of measurement of the market value of goods, services, and other transactions.

• Money provides a common measure for valuing goods and services, making it easier to compare their worth.

• This function of money allows for the recording and reporting of financial transactions in a consistent manner.

• Money as a standard of deferred payment is actually a significant function as it facilitates credit and future payments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Unit of Account:**

• It is a standard monetary unit of measurement of value/cost of goods, services, or assets.

• This allows for consistent accounting and economic reporting, making complex economic calculations possible.

• **Standard of Deferred Payment:**

• This function of money allows it to be used for payments that are to be made in the future.

• It is vital for the functioning of credit systems, as it provides the basis for loan and credit agreements.

• Contrary to what is mentioned in Option 2, modern economies heavily rely on this function for various financial instruments and credit facilities.

• **Store of Value:**

• Money can be saved and retrieved in the future, retaining its value over time.

• This function is important for savings and investments, as it ensures that money can be used for future transactions.

• **Medium of Exchange:**

• Money facilitates the buying and selling of goods and services, eliminating the inefficiencies of a barter system.

• It is universally accepted in exchange for goods and services, making transactions more efficient.

</ul

questions.question: The measures of money supply, namely, M1, M2, M3 and M4, in this order, indicate:

options.text: decreasing order of store of value

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** decreasing the order of liquidity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The money supply measures are used by central banks to monitor and control the amount of money in circulation in the economy.**
 
• ** M1 **includes the most liquid forms of money such as cash, demand deposits, and traveler's checks. It is considered a narrow measure of money supply.
 
• ** M2** includes M1 plus less liquid forms of money such as savings deposits, time deposits, and money market funds. It is considered a broader measure of money supply than M1.
 
• **M3 includes M2 plus large time deposits,** institutional money market funds, and other forms of less liquid assets. It is considered a broad measure of money supply.
 
• ** M4 includes M3 plus** all other forms of deposits such as certificates of deposit and commercial paper. It is considered the broadest measure of money supply.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Money)

 M1 (Narrow Money)
 Currency with the public + Deposit money of the public
 
 

 M2

 office savings banks

 (Broad

 Money)
 M3 is a measure of the money supply that includes M2 as well as large time deposits, institutional money market funds, short-term repurchase agreements (repo), and larger liquid assets.
 
 

 M4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **The money supply is defined as currency in circulation plus deposits in commercial banks in the most basic sense.**
 
• The total stock of money circulating in an economy is referred to as the money supply.
 
• In short, there are two types of money:
 
 
• Central bank money (MO).
 
• Commercial bank money (M1 and M3).
 
 
 
• **Central bank money** is designated as MO in money supply data, whereas commercial bank money is separated into M1 and M3 components. Post-office deposits are also** included in the M2 and M4 components.**

questions.question: Which of the following is issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Certificates of deposits**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Certificates of deposits** are issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value.
 
• They are a type of time deposit with a fixed maturity date and specified interest rate.
 
• Certificates of deposits are negotiable instruments, meaning they can be transferred from one party to another.
 
• They are often used by banks to raise funds from the market.
 
• The interest rate on certificates of deposits is generally higher than that on regular savings accounts, making them an attractive investment option for large investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Promissory notes** are written promises to pay a certain amount of money at a future date but are not issued at a discount.
 
• **Commercial papers** are unsecured short-term debt instruments issued by corporations, not commercial banks.
 
• **Treasury bills** are short-term government securities issued at a discount but by the government, not commercial banks.

questions.question:
Which of the following is an example of capital receipt?

A) Borrowings from World Bank to fund Project to Save Tigers

B) Sale of 30% stake in a PSU to private companies
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• **Capital receipt:-**

 
 
• It refers to the inflow of funds that are not generated from the regular operations of a business or organization.
 
• It can include sources such as sale of assets, borrowing, or capital contributions from shareholders or investors.
 
• Borrowings from World Bank to fund Project to Save Tigers - This is a capital receipt because it increases a liability (the amount borrowed needs to be repaid) and is intended for a capital project (funding a specific conservation project).
 
• Sale of 30% stake in a PSU to private companies is an example of capital receipt, as it is an inflow of funds from the sale of an asset.

questions.question: Which among the following is the oldest stock exchange in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The oldest stock exchange in India is the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), also known as the Stock Exchange, Mumbai.**
 
• It was established in** 1875** and is the **oldest stock exchange in Asia.**
 
• **The BSE is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra**, and has played a significant role in the development and growth of the Indian capital market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Multi-Commodity Exchange of India Ltd. (MCX) is not the oldest stock exchange in India**.

 
 
• It is actually a commodity derivatives exchange rather than a stock exchange.
 
• **MCX** was established in** 2003** and is headquartered in **Mumbai, India.**
 
• It primarily facilitates trading in commodity futures contracts,** including gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas, agricultural commodities, and more.**
 
• **MCX** provides a platform for market participants to trade and hedge their price risks in various commodities.
 
 
 
• **The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) is not the oldest stock exchange in India either.**
 
 
• It is another commodity derivatives exchange operating in India.
 
• **NCDEX** was established in **2003 **and is headquartered in **Mumbai, India.**
 
• It focuses on facilitating trading in agricultural commodities, such as** wheat, rice, maize, soybean, cotton, etc.**
 
• **NCDEX **provides a platform for market participants, including farmers, traders, and processors, to trade and hedge their price risks in agricultural commodities.
 
 
 
• **The National Stock Exchange (NSE)** is not the oldest stock exchange in India, but it is one of the major stock exchanges in the country.
 
 
• The **NSE** was established in** 1992** and is headquartered in** Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
 
• It is a leading stock exchange in India and provides a platform for trading various financial instruments, including **equities, derivatives, and exchange-traded funds (ETFs).**
 
• The** NSE** has played a crucial role in the modernization and development of the Indian capital market and is known for its advanced trading technology and extensive market reach.

questions.question: In India, ___________ fixes the CRR for the banks in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) fixes the CRR for the banks in the economy.
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is an important tool used by the RBI to manage liquidity in the banking system and control inflation.
 
• Cash reserve ratio (CRR): 
 
 
• It is a monetary policy tool used by central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), to regulate and control the money supply in the economy.
 
• CRR is the percentage of total deposits that commercial banks are required to keep as reserves with the central bank.
 
• It is a portion of the bank's demand and time liabilities.
 
• The primary objective of implementing CRR is to ensure the liquidity and stability of the banking system while controlling inflation and managing credit growth.
 
• When the central bank increases the CRR, it reduces the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks.
 
• This helps reduce excess liquidity in the economy by controlling inflationary pressures and curbing excessive credit expansion.
 
• On the other hand, **when **the **central bank decreases the CRR**, **it increases the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks**.
 
• This can stimulate credit growth, promote economic activity, and ease liquidity conditions in the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Reserve Bank of India (RBI):

 
 
• It is **India’s central bank**.
 
• In compliance with the terms of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, it was founded on April 1, 1935 in Calcutta.
 
• It was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
• Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• It also functions as the "lender of last resort" and is considered Banker to Banks.
 
• It regulates the issue of Bank notes and keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in India and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors the monetary policies through its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

questions.question: The net worth of any bank is equal to ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**assets (reserves + loans)** **- liabilities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To determine a **bank's net worth**, you **subtract its liabilities from its assets**.

 
 
• i.e. Total assets minus total liabilities.
 
 
 
• Assets: Everything the bank owns (loans, cash, investments, buildings, etc.)
 
• Liabilities: Everything the bank owes (customer deposits, loans payable, etc.)
 
• Net worth: The difference between assets and liabilities (what the bank truly owns after accounting for all its debts)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
In India, credit creation is done by:

A) Ministry of Finance

B) Reserve Bank of India

C) Commercial Banks
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India,** commercial banks** play a crucial role in credit creation, while the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) **regulates this process through various mechanisms such as the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), repo rate, and open market operations.
 
• Commercial banks generate credit by purchasing securities and extending loans, with the currency thus generated termed as credit money.
 
• Additionally, the RBI oversees the clearing of cheques among commercial banks and facilitates inter-bank fund transfers.
 
• Commercial banks are able to facilitate loans by leveraging the deposits acquired from the public. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Credit creation, **also referred to as "deposit creation," is the process wherein a country's money supply expands by utilizing a portion of customers' deposits to extend loans to businesses and individuals.
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), **India's central bank and regulatory authority, oversees the regulation of the Indian banking system. It operates under the ownership of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, and is tasked with controlling, issuing, and managing the supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• **The Ministry of Finance,** a department within the Government of India, focuses on managing the economy of India and functions as the Treasury. Its responsibilities encompass taxation, financial legislation, oversight of financial institutions, management of capital markets, administration of central and state finances, and formulation of the Union Budget.

questions.question: RBI defined M1 as CU + DD. What is DD?

options.text: Net demand deposits held by International banks only
Net demand deposits held by RBI
Net demand deposits held by SBI
Net demand deposits held by commercial banks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__**. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) defining M1, "DD" stands for Demand Deposits.**
 
• **Demand Deposits** represent the net demand deposits held by commercial banks.
 
• **Demand Deposits** are a type of bank account from which deposited funds can be withdrawn at any time without any notice to the bank.
 
• These types of accounts include checking accounts, savings accounts, or any other type of bank account that allows for the immediate withdrawal of funds.
 
• They are considered to be highly liquid assets and are included in the calculation of the** M1 money supply.**
 
• **Net Demand Deposits** would account for the total of these deposits held by a bank, minus any amounts that the bank has itself deposited with other banks.
 
• This gives a more accurate view of a bank's liquidity and the amount of money readily available in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) defines various monetary aggregates to measure the amount of money in circulation in the Indian economy.
 
• M1 money supply includes components such as:
 
 
• Currency **(notes and coins in circulation with the public and vault cash of banks) **- denoted as **CU.**
 
• **Demand Deposits of the public (DD) **with commercial banks.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding liquidity trap?

i. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely inelastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

ii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly inelastic.

iii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

iv. It is the point where speculative demand for money and the liquidity preference curves are not related.

options.text: Only Statements i and ii are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement iii is correct.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A liquidity trap is a situation where monetary policy becomes ineffective due to the zero lower bound on interest rates.**
 
• **​**Liquidity trap:
 
• A liquidity trap refers to a situation in which an increase in the money supply does not result in a fall in the interest rate but merely in addition to idle balances the interest elasticity of demand for money becomes infinite.
 
• Under normal conditions, an increase in money supply, resulting in excess cash balances, would cause an increase in bond prices, as individuals sought to acquire assets in exchange for money, and a corresponding fall in interest rates.
 
• The horizontal portion of the liquidity preference curve is referred to as the liquidity trap.
 
• In this portion of the curve, the demand for money is infinitely elastic with respect to the interest rate.
 
• Re­ductions in the interest rate, in this portion only, increase people’s desire to hold cash balances
 
• Statement 3 is correct as It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.
 
• In a liquidity trap, people prefer holding money regardless of the interest rate because they expect that the return on other assets will not be better. Therefore, the demand for money is infinitely elastic (it does not change with interest rates), and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly horizontal or elastic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__"**

 
• 
 
Speculative Demand for Money: In a liquidity trap, speculative demand for money is actually infinitely elastic, not inelastic. This means that people are willing to hold an unlimited amount of money at a particular low interest rate, because they expect interest rates to rise in the future, which would cause bond prices to fall.

 
 
• 
 
Liquidity Preference Curve: The curve becomes perfectly elastic (horizontal) at the liquidity trap, indicating that changes in the money supply will not affect interest rates because people prefer to hold money rather than invest in bonds.

 Thus, this statement is incorrect because it incorrectly describes speculative demand for money as infinitely inelastic

questions.question: Which of the following was the first microfinance institution in India, established in 1974?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SEWA Bank**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SEWA Bank, **established in **1974, **is one of India's** first microfinance institutions**.
 
• SEWA Bank was created with the primary aim of **providing access to financial services to self-employed women** who don't typically have access to traditional banking services due to lack of collateral and low incomes.
 
• The organization was built on the realization that poor women needed not just loans, but also** savings, insurance, and pension products** to withstand financial shocks and build assets.
 
• Besides financial services, SEWA Bank also provides** financial literacy training programs** for its members. This helps women understand better ways to manage and increase their income.
 
• SEWA Bank uses **peer-lending and community-monitoring techniques** to overcome problems related to moral hazard and adverse selection, which generally make lending to poor households and small businesses risky and costly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suryoday Small Finance Bank Ltd.:**

 
 
• **Suryoday Small Finance Bank (SSFB)** is one of the leading Small Finance Banks (SFB) in India having started operations in** 2017**.
 
• Even before obtaining its banking license from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), its parent organization, **Suryoday Micro Finance, **had been serving the unbanked and underbanked population **since 2009.**
 
• Apart from providing basic savings and deposit products, Suryoday offers loans to underserved segments of society, like microloans for women, affordable housing loans, and loans for small and micro enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Asirvad Micro Finance Limited:**
 
 
• Asirvad Microfinance Ltd is one of the leading **NBFC - Microfinance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs)** in India, having begun its operations** in 2007 in South India.**
 
• The company provides **microloans to women** from economically weaker sections who lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• Asirvad's primary mission is to empower women and their families financially through the provision of timely credit for both productive purposes and family welfare.
 
 
 
• **Bandhan Financial Services Pvt Ltd:**
 
 
• Bandhan Financial Services Pvt Ltd started as a** microfinance institution** in **2001**, catering to the dual objectives of poverty alleviation and women empowerment in India.
 
• Bandhan was among the first microfinance institutions in India transition to a full-service bank - t**he Bandhan Bank, which started in 2015** under the regulation of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• Bandhan Bank today serves millions of customers across India, offering services ranging from basic savings and deposit products to sophisticated corporate banking products.

questions.question: As per ’Basel III: A global regulatory framework for more resilient banks and banking systems’ released in December 2010, banks will be required to hold a capital conservation buffer of ______ of risk weighted assets (RWAs) in the form of common equity to withstand future periods of stress.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Basel III** is a set of international banking regulations developed by the Bank for International Settlements in order to promote stability in the international financial system.
 
• The **Basel Committee** published the Basel III rules text in **December 2010.**
 
• It covers the worldwide regulatory criteria on bank capital adequacy and liquidity that were agreed upon by the Governors and Heads of Supervision and adopted by the** G20 Leaders** at their November summit in Seoul.
 
• To withstand future periods of stress, banks will be required to keep a capital conservation buffer of **2.5%**__ of risk-weighted assets (RWAs) in the form of common equity under Basel III.
 
• The results of the Committee's complete **quantitative impact research** were also released (QIS).
 
• **Nout Wellink** was the Chairman of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
 
• Basel Committee on Banking Supervision examines and proposes ways to reconfigure global banking regulations.
 
• The Committee estimated that Group 1 banks in aggregate would have had a shortfall of €577 billion at the end of 2009.
 
• The Basel III accord increased the minimum Basel III capital requirements for banks from 2% in Basel II to 4.5% of common equity, as a percentage of the bank’s risk-weighted assets.
 
• In order to be Basel compliant, there is additionally a 2.5% buffer capital requirement, bringing the total minimum requirement to 7%.
 
• When banks are in financial distress, they can use the buffer, but doing so can result in even more financial constraints when it comes to paying dividends.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding microfinance?

options.text: Micro finance organizations (MFIs), are Banks that provide micro financial services.
Other than Banks, Micro finance organizations (MFIs) are organizations that provide micro financial services.
Micro finance has the provision of giving loans to micro, small and medium enterprises.
RBI is the regulatory body for micro finance institutions (MFIs).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro finance organizations (MFIs), are Banks that provide micro financial services.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Microfinance:-**

 
 
• It is a financial service that provides small loans, savings, and other financial services to low-income individuals or small businesses who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs) are organizations that offer microfinance services. These organizations can be banks or non-banking institutions.**
 
• Microfinance is important in promoting financial inclusion and reducing poverty by providing access to credit and other financial services to those who are excluded from traditional banking services.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the regulatory body for MFIs in India.

questions.question:
Which of the following does NOT create any corresponding liability for the government?

a. Revenue receipts

b. Capital receipts
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (a)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Receipts**

 
 
• **Revenue receipts** are defined as **those receipts that neither increase a government's liabilities nor decrease its assets**.
 
• They are **routine and ongoing in nature**, and the government receives them as **part of daily operations**.
 
• **Taxes and other levies collected by the Centre, interest and dividends received on investments, and fees and charges paid to the government for services** are all considered revenue receipts.
 
• Revenue receipts must meet the** following two requirements**:
 
 
• **No liability:** The** government is not liable for any revenue received**. For example, unlike borrowings, taxes received by the government do not result in any liabilities for it.
 
• **No asset reduction: **The **amount of assets owned by the government does not decrease as a result of revenue**. Therefore, because the sale of the share reduced the government's assets, it is not possible for it to report the earnings from the sale of the stake as revenue.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Receipts**

 
 
• **Receipts that create liabilities or decrease financial assets are referred to as capital receipts**.
 
• **Incoming monetary flows** are also referred as Capital receipts. 
 
• Both **debt and non-debt capital receipts** are possible.
 
• Capital receipts are significantly **influenced by loans from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), foreign governments, and the general public**.
 
• The** government's estimated capital receipts for the 2020–21 financial year were Rs. 1,074,306 crore**.
 
• While the **actual capital receipts for the 2018–19 Budget were Rs 763,518 crore**, the **revised **projections for the **2019–20 Budget came in at Rs 772,529 crore**.

questions.question: A type of loan that allows borrowers to make low payments in the initial phases but repayment of the balance amount in lump sum at maturity is known as _______.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Balloon Mortgage**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** In this type of loan,** borrowers make low payments** for a **certain period of time** and then **pay off the remaining balance** in **one large lump sum, or "balloon" payment**, at the **end of the loan term.**

**Initial Low Payments:**

 
• Balloon loans typically have lower initial payments compared to traditional loans.
 
• This is because these payments are primarily based on the interest of the loan, not the principal.

**Lump Sum Payment:**

 
• The defining feature of a balloon loan is the large "balloon" payment due at the end of the loan term.
 
• This payment covers the remaining principal of the loan.

**Short Term: **

 
• Balloon loans usually have shorter terms than traditional installment loans.
 
• The term is often 5 to 7 years, but the balloon payment is based on what the balance would be after a longer term, often 30 years.

**Risk of Default:**

 
• There is a higher risk of default with balloon loans.
 
• If borrowers cannot make the large balloon payment at the end of the term, they may need to refinance the loan, sell the asset, or default on the loan.

**Common in Real Estate:**

 
• Balloon loans are often used in real estate transactions, particularly for commercial properties or short-term real estate investments.
 
• They can also be used for personal loans and auto loans.

questions.question: As of 2022, what was the highest-denomination currency note printed by the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹10,000.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The highest denomination note ever printed by the Reserve Bank of India was the **₹10,000 note.**
 
• The ₹10,000 note was** first introduced in 1938.**
 
• It was **demonetized in January 1946** but was **again introduced in 1954.**
 
• The ₹10,000 note was **finally demonetized again in the year 1978.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **₹500 Note:**

 
 
• The first ₹500 note was introduced in **1987** to contain the volume of banknotes in circulation due to inflation.
 
• On** 8th November 2016,** the **old ₹500 note was demonetised alongside the ₹1,000 note** to combat black money, counterfeiting, and corruption.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India introduced a **new ₹500 note**, in what is called the Mahatma Gandhi New Series from **10th November 2016.** The features of this new series include a depiction of the** Red Fort – a historical Indian monument – and a portrait of Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
 
 
• **₹1,000 Note:**
 
 
• The ₹1,000 note was **first introduced in 2000.**
 
• Like the ₹500 note, the ₹1,000 note was **demonetised on 8th November 2016** with the aim of curbing black money, counterfeiting, and corruption.
 
• However, the ₹1,000 note has** not been reintroduced**.
 
 
 
• **₹2,000 Note:**
 
 
• This note was launched almost immediately after the demonetisation of the ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes **on 8th November 2016.**
 
• It features a portrait of Mahatma Gandhi, like the ₹500 note, and the reverse side displays an image of the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), also known as Mangalyaan, highlighting India's first venture into interplanetary space.

questions.question: Proportional taxes would help to reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier because ______.

options.text: MPC does not have any role in it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**taxes reduce the MPC.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Proportional taxes:-**

 
 
• A proportional tax is one where everyone pays the same percentage of their income in taxes. This means that as income increases, so does the amount of tax paid.
 
• It would help to reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier because taxes reduce the MPC.
 
• The MPC, or marginal propensity to consume, is the fraction of additional income that a person or household spends. When taxes increase, disposable income decreases, which in turn reduces the MPC.
 
• By reducing the MPC, proportional taxes can help to stabilize the economy by dampening the effects of fluctuations in autonomous expenditure, such as changes in investment or government spending.
 
• Other types of taxes, such as regressive taxes (where lower-income people pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes) or progressive taxes (where higher-income people pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes), could have different effects on the MPC and the autonomous expenditure multiplier.
